procedural_matters: NZL 3521 was represented by Bella Jenkins.
POL 3320 was represented by Weronika Grala.
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 5 knots ofwind and flat water.
NZL 3521 and POL 3320 were sailing upwind on convergingcourses with NZL 3521 sailing on starboard tack und POL 3320 on port tack.
When the distance between NZL 3521 and POL 3320 was 3 boat lengths POLasked if she could go in front of NZL 3521 and NZL 3521 denied.
When the distance between NZL 3521 and POL 3320 was 0.5 boat lengths NZL 3521 changed course to leeward.
There was contact between the spinnaker pole of NZL 3521 and theside of POL 3320 10 centimeters in front of the stern.
conclusions: POL 3320 on port tack failed to keep clear of NZL 3521 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
POL 3320 did not avoid contact with NZL 3521 even though it wasreasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
When it became clear that POL 3320 was not keeping clear it wasreasonably possible for NZL 3521, the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with POL 3320. NZL 3521 broke RRS 14(a).
Since NZL 3521 was right-of way boat and the contact did notcause damage or injury, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(c) for breakingRRS 14.
